quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Give you an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders for a better view.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to see where you are going. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They alert riders to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving around so you can focus on riding. Passengers should board only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle needs to lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, riding curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: To be seen better at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to help other drivers see you at intersections. Choose a lane position that helps oncoming traffic spot you. Keep a space cushion to escape danger if needed. Do not assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you NOT move to the far side of your lane away from the passing driver?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to finish the pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane could encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that tell you about rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
There is no single best lane position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position for all situations.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always unsafe. Choose a lane position based on your riding conditions. Make sure you have enough space around you and other drivers can see you.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right when using a three-wheeled motorcycle or sidecar?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is on the right side of a motorcycle. If you ride too far right, the sidecar can leave the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the right rear wheel can also go off the road edge if you get too close to the right side.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group
Right behind the leader
Near the back of the group
At the very end of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, right behind the leader. This way they will not have to struggle to keep up with the group. Experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely
Block all air from passing through
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath
Limit your side vision

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, give you clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: What may you need to adjust on your motorcycle before carrying a passenger?

options.text: The shocks
The handlebars
The brakes
The throttle

questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks for this weight. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance, what should you do?

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle ahead of you
Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead of you
Drive on the shoulder of the road
Have someone else ride your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead of you
questions.explanation: When stopping takes longer than normal, increase your distance behind other vehicles. Use at least a three-second following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: When it is raining, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane
Pull off the road and wait for the rain to stop
In the tire tracks left by cars
Ride faster

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the road is very slippery. Oil from cars has not yet washed away. Riding in the tire tracks left by cars is safest. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn
Windburn
Chapped lips
Dehydration

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and parts of the motorcycle. Good clothes also provide extra protection if you crash.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes
Brake hard on the front brake to keep the tire from locking
Use only the rear brake
Use one brake at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use light pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should you do?

options.text: Never use a staggered formation
Put inexperienced riders at the back
Do not use your mirrors
Do not follow too closely to other riders

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not follow too closely to other riders
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Check your mirrors often. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders.

questions.question: Where does debris and oil from cars collect in a traffic lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Where motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Where most accidents happen.
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of the lane. You may also find other hazards there, like manhole covers.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who try to share the lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side.
The center.
The right side.
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: The best lane position depends on road and traffic conditions. Change your position to create more space around you and to help other drivers see you better.

questions.question: What formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?

options.text: Pyramid.
Staggered.
Single-file.
Compressed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, entering curves, or getting on or off a highway. A staggered formation works best on straight roads because it keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. The driver may not see the hazard ahead that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light if you need to slow down where drivers might not expect it.
